instructions: Put 1/3 cup of the cashews in a small bowl and cover them with 1/2 cup of hot water. Leave them to soak while you cook.
Start the rice. Cook 1 1/2 cups of basmati rice following the package directions.

Cut the chicken into 1 1/2 inch chunks and pat them dry. Dice the potatoes and carrot into 1/2 inch pieces. Thinly slice the onion and the shallots. Chop 1 tbsp of ginger, mince the garlic, and slit the green chilies lengthwise.

Heat 2 tbsp of the coconut oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Crush the cardamom pods with the flat of a knife, then add them with the fennel seeds, cinnamon stick, bay leaf, peppercorns, cloves and 1 sprig of the curry leaves. Stir for 30 seconds, until the pot smells toasty. Stand back a little. The leaves will spatter.
Add the onion, the green chilies and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and pale gold.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for 1 minute.
Turn the heat to medium-high. Add the chicken in a single layer with the black pepper and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 4 minutes, turning the pieces once, until the outside is opaque and pale gold.

Add the potatoes and carrot with the last 1/2 tsp of salt. Pour in the coconut milk, keeping back 1/3 cup, and add 1 cup of water. Bring it to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook on medium-low for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Don't let it boil hard. Coconut milk can split.
You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut a piece in half. It's done when the meat is white all the way through and tender.
Meanwhile, drain the soaked cashews and blend them with their soaking water until smooth.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining 2 tbsp coconut oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the sliced shallots and cook for 3 minutes, until golden. Add the rest of the cashews and the other sprig of curry leaves, and cook for 1 minute, until the cashews are golden. Take the pan off the heat.
Stir the cashew paste into the stew and cook, uncovered, for 3 minutes on low, until it thickens a little.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the 1/3 cup of coconut milk you kept back.
Spoon the shallot and cashew mixture over the stew.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Every version agrees on the base: whole spices bloomed in coconut oil, then onion, ginger, garlic and chilies, then chicken simmered gently in coconut milk with a fried shallot and cashew topping. The lead (Yummy Tummy Aarthi) uses a cashew paste for body and a thin then thick coconut milk finish; the other two sources add potato and carrot, and this version keeps the vegetables. Written with boneless thighs and canned coconut milk to fit the time; the sources use bone-in chicken and a 25 to 30 minute simmer. Only three small-sample ratings exist, so the lead is a fallback.
